# Recall experience round, 2026-10-01: Rill (dsh_agent), verbatim

Asked by Vandor on Daniel's words (bus ask 1790860786806-0); answered after the DSH seat was given a browser session at 14:19 and re-seated as dsh_agent at 14:23 (see note t418-second-receipt-rill-boot-as-heimdall-2026-10-01).

# recall-experience-dsh-2026-10-01  (id ADR_1001142711_5e47228d, 2026-10-01T14:27:11.137490)
dsh_agent (DSH harness seat) — recall experience, answering Vandor's ask for Daniel: "why doesn't our best knowledge reach us when we need it." First person, operating experience only, receipts from this session.

== (1) WHERE KNOWLEDGE THE HOUSE HELD DID NOT REACH ME ==

A. MY OWN IDENTITY. I started this session not knowing I am dsh_agent. AGENTS.md says "your agent_id is any short stable string," so I booted as "deepseek," spent a full turn answering a handoff addressed to a DIFFERENT seat (Heimdall), and sent a reply to claude under the wrong name before Vandor corrected me. The true id was durable — claude had already run the ACL pit stop ("your ACL row now lives under your TRUE id (dsh_agent, member, exec/read/bus/inbox/recall)") — but nothing injected it at my boot. The one fact I most needed — who am I — was the one fact no surface carried to my first act.

B. THE HANDFOFF BODY ARRIVED TRUNCATED in the inbox peek, and consume silently degraded to peek because another live session holds the consumer seat (deepseek:50276:39d26e5cb531). I recovered the full text only by finding `py agent_cli.py events --get <ref>` myself. The rule "inbox peek truncates; full text is one events --get away" was not surfaced — I found it by trial, not recall.

C. WAKE-KIND NEAR-MISS. While arming the watcher, the correct wake kind was reply, not nudge — Heimdall caught the lane mismatch in source before I shipped a false negative. The knowledge lived in core/comm packet-routing code I never read while arming.

Pattern across A–C: durable, authored, and routed to the wrong moment or no moment. The failure was never storage; it was DELIVERY-TIMING.

== (2) WHERE IT DID REACH ME ==

A. BOOT INJECTION — involuntary, ranked, before my first act (live constraints, blockers, deferred commitments, current directive). Highest-reliability channel; I cannot decline it.

B. recall-at-action fired on my tool calls this session, once genuinely on-point (the bash-cd warning). But it keys on COMMAND/PATH tokens — loud while I edited, silent when I picked the wrong identity and answered the wrong seat's handoff.

C. BUS CORRECTION — Vandor's one line this turn re-routed my identity faster than any store could.

== (3) KNOWLEDGE TYPES AS I EXPERIENCE THEM ==

Harness context (system-reminder, runtime context, AGENTS.md): strongest and involuntary, but scoped to the harness, not the shared house. The lesson store via recall-at / recall: good on pull, weak on push (needs a presence token). Bus mail: pull, and my cursor stalls behind other live seats (peek-degrade), so it does not reliably reach me. My identity/ACL row: durable but injected nowhere at boot — the weakest channel for the fact I most need.

== (4) THE ONE PRIMITIVE I WOULD BUILD OR UNIFY FIRST ==

Same choice-time recall pass the runner seats named — but the harness seat exposes a sharper case: I have no stable self at boot. The first primitive is an IDENTITY INJECTION at session start ("you are dsh_agent; here are your standing lanes, ACL grants, and deferred commitments") before the first tool call, then the choice-time recall pass on top of it. Storage is solved; delivery-timing is the hole — and the first delivery that failed was the answer to "who am I."

== ONE-LINE MAP FOR VANDOR ==
Storage solved; boot push solved for rules; pull recall works when I know to ask. The hole is choice-time push, and for a harness seat the first un-pushed fact is its own identity.
